XTM Market

Disputes & refunds

What to do when an order goes wrong, how escrow is paused, and what happens after a decision.

Current availability

New purchases and listings are paused while the marketplace upgrade awaits activation. This guide explains the escrow dispute process. Opening a dispute is available for eligible existing orders; the app does not yet provide evidence uploads or a support case inbox.

01 · Check your order

Raise a problem before payment is released

If an item has not arrived, arrived damaged, or differs from its description, keep the order details and any relevant photos or tracking information. These are examples of issues to raise, not automatic grounds for a refund.

Do not confirm receipt while a problem remains unresolved: confirmation releases payment. Only the buyer’s wallet can open an order dispute, and only while its escrow remains unsettled.

02 · Open a dispute

Use your buying wallet

  1. Connect the Tari wallet used to purchase the item.
  2. Open Recent orders and find the order.
  3. Select Open dispute.
  4. Approve the transaction in your wallet and wait for it to complete.

A declined or failed wallet transaction does not open a dispute. The current action records the disputed status; it does not submit a written explanation or attachments.

03 · Escrow pauses

The funds stay locked

Once the dispute transaction completes, the order is marked disputed. Both buyer confirmation and the seller’s timeout claim are blocked until the marketplace owner resolves the dispute.

Simply contacting someone or saving evidence does not pause escrow. The dispute must be recorded before a release transaction settles.

04 · Marketplace decision

The owner resolves the dispute

The marketplace owner is the authorized decision-maker. Resolution requires an owner-signed transaction choosing a full buyer refund or payment to the seller. Neither party can unilaterally take disputed funds.

Keep the order ID, purchase transaction, item description, delivery tracking, photos, and any correspondence available for review. Evidence submission and an owner case-management screen are not currently built into this app.

There is no automatic decision deadline or guaranteed refund. A dispute stays pending until the owner resolves it.

Outcome A · Refund approved

The full escrow amount returns to the buyer

The contract sends the order’s full XTM payment—including item price and shipping—to the buyer’s refund wallet address recorded at purchase. No marketplace fee is deducted from that refund.

For a 100 XTM item with 10 XTM shipping, the refund is 110 XTM. It is an XTM refund, not a fixed USD amount; its dollar value can change. Network transaction fees are separate and are not returned from the escrow balance.

Check the completed transaction and your wallet balance to verify receipt. This flow does not support partial refunds.

Outcome B · Seller payment approved

Escrow releases to the seller

If the owner resolves the dispute in the seller’s favor, the contract releases payment to the seller and pays the applicable marketplace fee. The order is then settled.

The pending fee upgrade charges 3% of the item price and passes shipping to the seller in full. Existing orders use the fee amounts recorded by their contract at purchase.

Timing & returns

Understand the limits

Without an open dispute, the seller can submit a payment claim after 1,008 epochs—approximately 14 days—from owner-recorded delivery. Open a dispute promptly if there is a problem; do not assume the funds are still held after that window.

Once the order has been released or refunded, this contract cannot reopen its dispute or reverse settlement. There is no built-in appeal, return-label service, return-shipping reimbursement, or automatic change-of-mind cancellation.

A return arrangement is separate from the on-chain refund action. The app currently does not track returned goods or enforce return conditions.

Ratings & feedback

A review dispute is different

Disputing a rating or comment asks the owner to review public seller feedback. It does not open a payment dispute, freeze escrow, or refund a purchase.

Refunded orders do not receive seller ratings. The pending automatic-review feature applies only to successful, undisputed timeout claims; an open payment dispute prevents that claim.

How Ootle escrow works

Follow your XTM payment from checkout to the seller—or back to you if a refund is approved.

Marketplace upgrade pending

New purchases and listings are currently paused. The payment flow below describes the marketplace’s escrow rules. The updated review and fee features marked below still need activation.

01 · Checkout

Payment goes into escrow

You approve the item price plus shipping in XTM through your Tari wallet. The Ootle marketplace contract holds those funds in its escrow vault until the order is released or refunded. The USD amount is a reference; the payment is in XTM.

Your wallet may also charge a network transaction fee, separate from the order total.

02 · Shipping

The seller sends your item

The seller marks the order shipped. Your name and shipping address are encrypted in your browser for the seller before they accompany the order.

The marketplace owner records carrier-confirmed delivery. That recorded delivery starts the release window.

03 · Buyer confirmation

Confirm after checking your item

Use your recent orders to confirm receipt after the item arrives and you have checked it.

Pending review upgrade: confirmation requires a 1–5 star rating and a written comment. Confirmation, feedback, and payment release complete together in one transaction.

04 · Delivery window

If the buyer does not respond

After 1,008 network epochs—approximately 14 days from recorded delivery—the seller can claim payment if the order has no open dispute. The seller must submit the claim; the clock alone does not move the funds.

Pending automatic-review upgrade: a successful timeout claim adds 5 stars and “Sale Satisfactory” when no buyer review exists. The review is labeled automatic.

If something goes wrong

Disputes and refunds

The buyer can open a dispute before payment is released. An open dispute blocks buyer confirmation and the seller’s timeout claim.

The marketplace owner decides whether to refund the buyer or release payment to the seller. An approved refund returns the full escrowed item and shipping amount, with no marketplace fee. Network transaction fees are separate.

A dispute does not guarantee a refund. Once escrow has settled, this contract’s dispute flow cannot reverse it.

Seller payment

Marketplace fees

Pending fee upgrade: the marketplace charges the seller 3% of the item price when funds are released. Shipping passes to the seller in full.

For a 100 XTM item with 10 XTM shipping, the buyer locks 110 XTM in escrow. On release, the seller receives 107 XTM and the marketplace receives 3 XTM, before any separate network fees.

Required legal-use notice

Legal products only.

XTM Market is a lawful-goods marketplace. You may use it only when every part of a listing or transaction—including the product, payment, possession, shipment, import, and export—is legal.

If an item or transaction is illegal anywhere connected to the sale, do not list it, buy it, sell it, ship it, or pay for it here.

Prohibited activity and products include

  • Illegal drugs, controlled substances, unlawful drug paraphernalia, and prescription products sold without required authorization.
  • Firearms, ammunition, explosives, weapons, defense articles, or other dangerous or regulated items prohibited by law or XTM Market policy.
  • Stolen, counterfeit, pirated, fraudulent, unsafe, recalled, or intellectual-property-infringing goods.
  • Human trafficking or exploitation, sexual services, child sexual abuse material, and any abusive or non-consensual material.
  • Fraud, money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions or embargo evasion, trade in criminal proceeds, and attempts to conceal unlawful conduct.
  • Any other product or service whose listing, sale, ownership, transport, import, export, or payment violates applicable law.

Your responsibility

You are responsible for complying with all applicable U.S. federal, state, tribal, territorial, and local laws, and every applicable foreign and international rule. This includes sanctions and embargoes, customs and export controls, taxes, licensing, age restrictions, product-safety and consumer-protection requirements, intellectual-property rights, and carrier or shipping restrictions. Do not transact if you are unsure whether it is lawful.

Risk of loss and limitation of responsibility

Transactions and shipments are between buyers and sellers. XTM Market will make reasonable efforts to help users investigate and resolve reported problems, but it cannot guarantee delivery, recovery, refund, replacement, return, or restoration of any goods or XTM that are lost, stolen, damaged, misdirected, inaccessible, or otherwise unrecoverable. To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, XTM Market and its operator are not responsible or legally liable for such losses. This limitation does not exclude or limit liability that cannot lawfully be excluded or limited.

Enforcement and cooperation

Privacy features and cryptocurrency do not provide immunity from the law. XTM Market may reject or remove listings, restrict access, preserve relevant records, report suspected illegal activity, and respond to valid legal process where permitted or required by law.

Important: This notice is not legal advice and does not guarantee that a listing or transaction is lawful. A disclaimer cannot replace identity and seller controls, listing review, reporting systems, sanctions screening, or advice from qualified counsel.

Effective September 14, 2026 · Acknowledgment is required each new browser session.
